description: On the night of May 17, 2024, Youssef was found dead in his home in the Medina district of Rabat.

His phone was recovered at the scene and immediately placed inside a Faraday container — a shielded enclosure that blocks all wireless signals so the device cannot be tracked, accessed, or wiped remotely.
Two suspects were near the house that night. It is up to you to cross-reference the digital traces and decide what each of them came to do.
objectives: How digital forensics connects different types of data to solve a real case.
The importance of isolating a device to preserve evidence.
How phone data, network data, and account data can be cross-referenced.
How timelines, locations, and behavior help identify suspects.
That even when someone tries to destroy evidence, digital traces can reveal the truth.

witness.summary: The housekeeper arrives early, notices unusual lights and no answer, then calls the police.

karim.summary: Drug deal contact. Upset about the deal, says he is coming over. Was invited in to talk.

samir.summary: Victim's friend. Drunk that night, not invited, came over anyway.

evidence.title: Victim's Phone
evidence.body: Recovered at crime scene (Victim's house). Placed at police station.

evidence.title: Conversations
evidence.body: Threads with the housekeeper, Karim, and Samir reveal motive, invitations and the early-morning alert.

evidence.title: Cellular Network Data
evidence.body: Provided by telecom provider. Includes call logs, SMS metadata, and cell tower triangulation.

evidence.title: Google Account Data
evidence.body: From the victim's laptop found at the house. Shows logins and remote deletion attempts.

paragraphs: The victim's phone was placed in a Faraday container immediately after recovery to block all wireless signals.
During transport to the police station, two remote deletion attempts were made via the Google account. Both attempts were blocked.
Faraday isolation preserves evidence by preventing remote access, tracking, and data deletion.

cards.title: Two suspects entered the house
cards.body: Karim came over after an argument about a drug deal — he was upset, but he was invited in to talk it out.

cards.title: And the other one came drunk
cards.body: Samir was drunk, not invited, and came over anyway. He was looking for drugs and may still have been upset about a girl.

cards.title: It's up to you to decide
cards.body: Forensic isolation preserved the phone, the cellular pings placed both men on site, and the blocked Google attempts came from Karim's area. The traces are clear — the motive is yours to interpret.
